headline: Pangenome frameworks reveal hidden diversity in cereal gene families and repeat arrays
label: Pangenome Reference Resources
summary: Panel-level and repeat-resolved references are replacing single-genome views for resolving structural and gene-family diversity.
synthesis: The dominant thread is a move from single-genome references toward pangenome-level representations that expose diversity invisible to any one assembly. A domain-defined pangene framework across four cereals, covering roughly 500 gene families, reports pangene membership rising 59-264% over single-genome analyses. Yruler uses pangenome assemblies to measure human Y chromosome satellite arrays directly from sequencing reads, without alignment, reporting length, composition and dosage. TideCluster is reference-independent, clustering tandem repeat arrays from genome assemblies into family catalogs with consensus monomers for comparative and pangenomic analysis. What is new across these is quantification of diversity at the level of panels and repeat families rather than individual genomes. A maize and Brassica rapa study is related only through its use of genomic and epigenomic features, linking recombination rate and chromatin context to subgenome identity.
